videos.script: Lesson 1's hits prints a table and exits. That is right for a script. But a person often wants to look around: move down the list, open one path, go back. {{screen}} This lesson builds that screen with Bubble Tea. You press j, and the cursor moves. You press Enter, and one path is broken down by status code. {{loop}} Bubble Tea does it with a loop you never write. Your program is a value, called the model. Every key press becomes a message. One function, Update, turns the model and a message into the next model. Another, View, draws it. {{cmd}} Reading the log takes time, so it runs as a command, off to one side. Its result comes back as one more message, and the screen keeps answering while it runs. {{test}} Because the screen is only a function of the model, you can test it without a terminal. Send the messages, then compare the text. {{limits}} The lesson ends with when not to draw a screen at all. A script, a pipe and a screen reader need the plain table. So hits browse checks for a terminal first, and sends everybody else to hits top.
